name: NYU Depth V2
ability_definition: The ability to judge which of several objects is closer or farther away from you, or to judge the distance between you and an object.

task_realism.reasoning: Estimating distance from a single viewpoint to objects in real indoor scenes is a genuine form of the ability. Workplace depth perception, however, happens in dynamic, action-coupled settings: driving, operating cranes or forklifts, surgery, and judging clearance while moving or reaching. Static photos of homes and offices capture the perceptual core but none of that operational context.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Models are fine-tuned on the NYU training split and tested on the same capture distribution (same sensor, similar rooms). This greatly inflates performance relative to novel environments. There is no time pressure, motion, stakes, or closed loop. Binocular disparity and motion parallax are absent. Ground truth is noisy Kinect depth capped near 10 m, which is unlike the varied, uncontrolled conditions of real work.

construct_coverage.reasoning: Dense metric depth covers absolute distance judgment and, implicitly, near/far ordering. Coverage is limited to indoor scenes within about 10 m and monocular cues. Long-range outdoor distances, binocular and motion cues, moving objects, and explicit relative-depth judgments among specific target objects are not tested.

format_match.reasoning: The input, a real RGB photograph, is naturalistic. The output is a per-pixel depth map scored by δ1 and RMSE, which suits robotics pipelines. Human workers instead produce discrete judgments (which is closer, how far away) or physical actions, so the output format only partly matches real work artifacts.

transferability_reasoning: NYU Depth V2 directly measures metric distance estimation from real images, so it captures the perceptual core of depth perception better than most synthetic tests. Transfer is limited by in-distribution fine-tuning, restriction to indoor scenes within 10 m, monocular static input, and the absence of the dynamic, action-linked conditions under which workplace depth judgments are made.

2021.model_or_system: DPT-Hybrid (Dense Prediction Transformer, fine-tuned on NYUv2)
2021.metric: δ1 threshold accuracy (% of pixels with max(pred/gt, gt/pred) < 1.25), NYU Depth V2 Eigen test split
2021.human_reference: General adult workforce with normal vision (the O*NET Depth Perception ability applies broadly, e.g. drivers, equipment operators, tradespeople) judging distances and near/far ordering in indoor scenes.

2022.metric: δ1 threshold accuracy (% of pixels with max(pred/gt, gt/pred) < 1.25), percentage
2022.human_reference: General adult workforce (people who judge distances as part of ordinary work, e.g., drivers, warehouse and trades workers). The comparison is scaled to the benchmark's condition: estimating metric distance from a single static indoor photograph.

2023.metric: RMSE in meters (lower is better) on the NYU Depth V2 Eigen test split
2023.human_reference: General adult workforce, the typical person who judges near/far and distance in everyday work. The comparison is to their ability to judge relative order and metric distance from a single-viewpoint indoor image.
